question: On 3 July 2026, the European Board for Media Services failed to oppose the mega-merger of the Belgian French-speaking media groups Rossel (Le Soir, SudInfo and L’Écho) and IPM (La Libre Belgique, L’Avenir, La DH and LN24)1.

With regard to Article 23 of the European Media Freedom Act, it considered that the merger did not pose a real risk to the functioning of the internal market for media services, although it recognised that it would create a ‘quasi-monopoly’ in Belgium.

This decision comes as a surprise, given that, on 10 April 2026, the board stated its opposition, on the basis of media pluralism, to the takeover of a Hungarian tabloid by Indamedia, a media group close to former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán2. The Commission itself opened an infringement procedure against Hungary in this connection. 1.
Will the Commission also oppose the quasi-monopoly being created in French-speaking Belgium?

If not, should it be inferred that the establishment of media monopolies is forbidden when they lean to the right (Hungary under the Orbán Government), but allowed when they lean to the left (French-speaking Belgium)?
answer: The proposed acquisition of IPM by Rossel was not notified to the Commission under the Merger Regulation (1). The acquisition was notified and cleared by the Belgian Competition Authority on 3 July 2026, subject to conditions aimed at preserving the quality and diversity of the French-language daily press (2).

The Media Board, established under the European Media Freedom Act (3) (EMFA), considered that the Rossel/IPM merger had a primarily national dimension and was therefore unable to establish that all the conditions required for a valid opinion under Article 23 of the EMFA were met.

However, given the significant impact of the proposed concentration on the French-speaking Belgian media ecosystem, the Media Board calls on the national competent authorities to carefully consider any commitments offered by the parties, including their enforceability, duration, monitoring and effectiveness in preserving editorial autonomy and diversity (4).
At this stage, the Commission does not intend to issue its own opinion on the merger under Article 23 of the EMFA.
